                    ### Question
                    A 35-year-old man comes to the physician because of a rash on the thigh for 10 days. He reports that the rash has been enlarging and is intensely itchy. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Options

opb. Erythrasma
opc. Pityriasis rosea
opd. Dermatophyte infection
ope. Tinea versicolor

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient is a 35-year-old man with an intensely itchy rash on the thigh that has been enlarging for 10 days, coinciding with the recent adoption of a stray dog. Given the acute onset and the context of potential zoonotic transmission, a dermatophyte infection (such as tinea corporis) is the most likely cause of the symptoms. Psoriasis is unlikely due to the acute nature of the rash, and erythrasma and pityriasis rosea are less consistent with the presentation. Evidence supports that dermatophyte infections are common in individuals with pets, confirming the reasoning that a dermatophyte infection is the most plausible diagnosis.
